extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature — professional scientists and researchers (anatomy/forensics, genetics, chemistry/physical chemistry, metrology, anthropometry/photography)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying evaluative criteria and methodological standards presented across short scientific letters, notes, and reviews (topics include skeletal identification, Mendelian interpretation, dye spectroscopy, portrait classification, and weights & measures). Useful for assessing methods, evidence, and reporting standards in short-form scientific communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cranial and pelvic features for sex determination
rubrics_metrics.description: On the evidence of the cranium alone the sex is obvious: mastoid processes typically masculine; the skull may be exceptionally capacious while the face disproportionately big. The pelvis exhibits the most characteristic masculine features: shape of the pubes and the pubo-ischial rami, the size and shape of the subpubic angle (67°), the form of the obturator foramen, the proportions of the pelvic cavity, and the shape of the iliac bones. The femur serves to demonstrate male sex by its size, inclination of shaft, and size of head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple skeletal regions (cranium, pelvis, femur) together; report measured angles (e.g., subpubic angle) and qualitative features (shape of rami, obturator foramen, iliac bones). Beware misquotations of comparative figures (the author notes an erroneous citation of female vs male angle ranges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age estimation from dentition and epiphyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Teeth unworn; three 'wisdom' teeth recently erupted and the fourth just emerging; a large number of epiphyses on ribs, vertebrae, clavicles, sternum, and pelvis were either separate or in process of joining—indicating bones of a person much younger than Queen Til's known age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use state of dental wear and stage of epiphyseal union across multiple bones to estimate biological age; compare to expected ages (e.g., 'about half the age' of a known adult). Report dental eruption status and which epiphyses are unfused or fusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish full osteological account with illustrative photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: A full account of the skeleton should be published, with photographs exhibiting the evidences of sex and age, and the points of similarity and dissimilarity to known comparative specimens (e.g., royal mummies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide photographic documentation that clearly shows diagnostic features used in determinations (angles, pelvic features, dentition, epiphyseal status) and include comparative plates to reference specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'bi-parental' in Mendelian inheritance
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Mendelian phenomena are possible only when reproduction is bi-parental' — the expression 'bi-parental' should not be taken too literally, since many Mendelian inheritance cases investigated use self-fertilisation (autogamy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing applicability of Mendelian principles, consider that Mendelian segregation can be observed in self-fertilising organisms; do not require strict external biparental mating as a precondition for Mendelian analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blended first cross is not a criterion of non‑Mendelian inheritance
rubrics_metrics.description: The appearance of a blended first cross is no criterion of non-Mendelian inheritance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid concluding non-Mendelian mechanisms solely from intermediate phenotypes in F1 crosses; perform further segregation analysis and experiments before rejecting Mendelian models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep definitions of characters flexible and favour experimental revision
rubrics_metrics.description: If an investigator rigidly defines 'characters' and does not keep an open mind, prepared to revise definitions in light of experimental evidence, there is risk of finding confusion instead of definite methods of inheritance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define characters operationally but be prepared to re-define them based on experimental segregation and analysis; prioritize experimental evidence over preconceptions when inferring modes of inheritance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require experimental evidence before asserting absence of segregation
rubrics_metrics.description: One should await the result of experimental evidence before accepting positive statements such as 'there is no segregation' (example: mulatto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make categorical claims about absence of segregation in complex cases (e.g., human mixed populations) without controlled experimental or strong population-genetic evidence; document what evidence supports such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on assuming cultivation causes variation vs revealing mutations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a mistake to deduce from the appearance of mutations under cultivation that cultivation actually causes them; the occurrence of mutations under cultivation is established, but the converse (that cultivation causes this kind of variation) lacks factual support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between conditions that reveal pre-existing variation and those that induce new variation; require direct evidence before asserting causation by cultivation or environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two types of dye‑solution absorption spectra (chemical vs resonance)
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain dyes the absorption spectrum in solution may be either (a) a characteristic absorption consisting of one or more narrow bands depending on the chemical structure of the dye molecule, or (b) a 'resonance' spectrum due to colloidal particles, much more remotely connected with chemical constitution; this spectrum is ill-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing dye solution spectra, consider whether narrow-band (molecular electronic transitions) or broad/resonance (colloidal aggregation) behaviour explains observed absorption; perform solvent and treatment tests to distinguish the two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonance spectrum: definition and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Resonance' spectrum denotes absorption exhibited by colloidal metal solutions, glasses, and certain photographically prepared films (references to Kirschner, Zsigmondy, Schaum & Schiœmann).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider resonance absorption mechanisms for colloidal systems and aggregates; cite and compare to known colloidal absorption literature when attributing broad/ill-defined bands to colloidal resonance effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental tests to distinguish colloidal vs molecular absorption
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: a pthacyanol dye gives in aqueous solution a flat, ill-defined absorption with colloidal characteristics; in alcohol and organic solvents the absorption becomes narrow-band and different; the narrow-band spectrum is also obtained by heating the aqueous solution to boiling point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test dye solutions in different solvents and after heating (e.g., boiling) to see whether spectral shape changes (colloidal → molecular). Use these behaviour patterns as diagnostic evidence of aggregation/colloidal state vs solvated molecular state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary portrait outline classification using six cardinal features
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuality of a portrait lies more in the relative positions of six cardinal features (tip of chin c, lower lip L, upper lip U, hollow between upper lip and nose m, tip of the nose n, hollow between nose and brow f) than in the connecting-line shapes. Representative points for these features can be determined by tangents and intersections to obtain a fundamental triangle CNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For silhouette/profile classification, determine six representative points via tangent constructions on tracing paper, form triangle CNF, and use these points as the basis for numerical description and comparison of portraits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate and triangulation methods for portrait measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions of the six cardinal points may be expressed either (1) by rectangular coordinates (YCY axis as Y and XCX as X) or (2) by triangulation (additional perpendicular NP from N to YCY); both methods have pros and cons depending on portrait scale and available instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose coordinate or triangulation approach according to scale and instrument; document method used. The author inclines to prefer coordinates overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale 'cents' and measurement precision in portrait lexiconisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Length CF divided into 100 equal parts called 'cents'; in a life-sized portrait 1 cent ~ roughly 1.25 mm (OCR uncertain) or ~1/20th of an inch (author's approximation). In experiments with 68 profiles differences of 3 cents in one or more measures distinguished nearly identical pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a standardized scale (e.g., CF=100 cents) for measurements; report units and approximate real-world equivalent; consider differences of ~3 cents as a threshold for distinctiveness in profiles of the studied scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexiconisation strategy and expected distinctiveness statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Lexiconise portraits by arranging measures between pairs of representative points in numerical order (analogous to dictionary order). In a sample of 68 profiles none had the same numerical formula; extrapolation suggests that in 1000 profiles ~667 would have clearly distinct formulae, with the remainder showing doubtful duplicates/triplicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lexicon-style ordered numerical descriptors of coordinates/angles to enable rapid search and identification in a portrait database; expect some duplicates in large populations, and quantify expected distinctiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity via dividing variability into nine equal parts
rubrics_metrics.description: For brevity, consider only the limits within which variability of each link most commonly occurs and divide the interval between these limits into 9 equal parts; then encode measurements as categories (1–9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compact representation is required, discretize continuous measures into nine bins representing typical variability ranges; record any values below/above limits as extreme categories; report binning scheme and limits used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard temperatures for verification of measures (Weights & Measures Regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of length are to be verified by comparison with a local standard at the 'normal' temperature, which is 61° F. for imperial measures. For imperial measures of capacity the standard temperature of their water contents is also 62° F.; for metric measures of capacity it is 4° C.; metric measures graduated at 15° C. (60° F.) may also be verified for chemical or pharmaceutical purposes or for volumetric estimations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When verifying measures, use the specified standard temperatures according to system and purpose; document temperature at verification and adjust or restandardize measures marked or graduated at particular temperatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing measures marked with a graduation temperature
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures marked with the temperature at which they are graduated must be tested against new or standardised measures at the same temperature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For temperature-marked measures, perform comparisons at that declared temperature; include calibration temperature in verification records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted weighing instruments and class markings for specific traders
rubrics_metrics.description: Traders such as dealers in precious metals/stones, retail chemists/druggists, and silk merchants may use (1) chemical and assay balances with means for relieving bearings and knife edges, (2) beam scales of lower order of sensitiveness/accuracy marked 'Class I B', and (3) instruments other than beam scales which satisfy requirements for Class B. The first and third types are not to be marked with a 'class'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure traders use only the permitted classes of instruments; verify that required design features (relieving bearings, knife edges) are present; apply correct class markings where mandated and withhold them where prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of adjusting contrivances not permanently fixed
rubrics_metrics.description: Nos. 69 and 78 of the regulations prohibit adjusting contrivances which are not permanently fixed to the weighing instrument, potentially rendering some analytical and assay balances ineligible for official stamping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect balances for removable adjustment mechanisms; if adjustments are not permanently fixed the instrument may fail for official stamping—advise traders accordingly and remove unstamped ineligible balances from trade premises to avoid liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition and test for counter weighing 'accelerating' machines
rubrics_metrics.description: Counter weighing machines of the 'accelerating' type are prohibited. It may be difficult to distinguish accelerating from vibrating instruments; the prescribed requirement is that the machine shall balance when unloaded. A practical test: when unloaded, if a pan pressed down and released causes the beam to oscillate about horizontal, it's vibrating; if a pan remains down and beam rests out of balance, it's accelerating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the unload-and-press test to classify machines; prohibit and remove accelerating-type counter machines from trade use; document test results during inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation and permitted uses of spring balances; re-stamping/grandfathering
rubrics_metrics.description: Spring balances are somewhat rigorously dealt with but may be permitted for ordinary trade; they are not restricted solely to parcel/passenger weighing as on the Continent. Weights, measures, and instruments presently stamped and in use but not compliant with new regulations may continue in use for prescribed periods and may be re-stamped from time to time (except a particular type of spring balance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply transitional allowances for existing stamped instruments per regulation timelines; inform traders of re-stamping possibilities and exceptions; restrict newly introduced non-compliant spring balances as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of currently legal denominations and prohibition of certain small weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix 2 contains a list of all denominations of weights and measures currently legal in the country. It is noted that weights of 1 grain, frequently employed by chemists for compounding drugs, are not legal for use in trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the official denomination list when preparing trade weights/measures; do not use non-legal denominations (e.g., 1 grain) for trade purposes; provide advisory information to chemists and others to switch to legal denominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication quality criteria for archaeological monographs (book production/plates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clarendon Press produced the book in sumptuous style: broad page and good type; title-page exemplary. Faults: photographs in first volume printed on paper too thin, giving half-tones a cheap appearance; some plates (first eighteen of second volume) similarly thin; one plate printed upside down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or producing archaeological monographs, assess overall typographic quality, paper stock appropriateness for halftone plates, correct orientation of illustrations, and the fidelity of color plates (text praises colored plates reproducing textiles). Note that printing quality affects perceived scholarly value.
